prov.heading: Provision For Credit Losses
prov.text: A recovery of provision for credit losses of $69,000 was recorded for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The Company recorded a $399,000 recovery of provision for credit losses on loans primarily due to a decline in loan principal of $17.8 million and favorable changes in portfolio concentrations and improvement for individually assessed loans. This was partially offset as the provision for credit losses on unfunded commitments was $330,000 and was primarily due to a $10.8 million increase in unfunded commitments and an increase in the loss rate for construction and land development unfunded commitments. This compared to a provision for credit losses of $259,000 recorded for the three months ended September 30, 2025 as the provision for credit losses on loans was $336,000 and was primarily due to additional reserves required for overall loan growth, changes in qualitative factors and an addition to individually assessed loans requiring specific reserves, partially offset by favorable changes in portfolio concentrations and the calculated loss rate. This was partially offset by a $77,000 recovery for credit losses on unfunded commitments due to a decrease in unfunded commitments.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text: Noninterest expense increased $1.1 million, or 11.8%, to $10.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $9.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Salaries and benefits increased $604,000 primarily due to revenue producing treasury and commercial banking personnel additions, merit increases and higher benefit compensation costs. Data processing expense increased $345,000 due to the implementation of enhanced treasury and commercial banking platforms in late 2025 and early 2026. Contracted services increased $127,000 due to outsourced information security and treasury consulting services.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense increased $353,000, or 5.7%, to $6.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $6.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

• Interest expense on deposits increased $82,000, or 1.4%, to $5.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $5.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Average interest-bearing deposit balances increased $113.5 million, or 11.1%, to $1.13 billion as of September 30, 2026 compared to $1.02 billion as of September 30, 2025, primarily as the Bank grew core banking relationships and onboarded Specialty Treasury clients. The increase in average balances accounted for a $622,000 increase in interest expense. This was partially offset as the cost of interest-bearing deposits decreased 20 bps to 2.06% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 2.26% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 due to the Federal Reserve federal funds target rate decreases since September 2025. The decrease in the cost of interest-bearing deposits accounted for a $540,000 decrease in interest expense.

• Interest expense on borrowed funds increased $271,000, or 62.7%, to $703,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $432,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense was $497,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to a $1.3 million tax benefit for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This change was driven by an increase in pre-tax income to $5.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to a $7.0 million loss for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was 8.5%. The minimal effective tax rate resulted primarily from a $462,000 federal income tax benefit related to the purchase during the third quarter of a $7.7 million 2025 renewable energy tax credit and an increase in low-income housing tax credits. This compared to an effective tax benefit rate of 18.9% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 due to the prior period loss on the sale of securities as part of the Company’s balance sheet repositioning strategy.

net.text: Net income was $5.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $11.0 million compared to a net loss of $5.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

capex.text: Other than loan commitments and standby and performance letters of credit, we do not have any off-balance sheet arrangements that have or are reasonably likely to have a significant current or future effect on our financial condition, revenues, expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures, or capital resources that are material to investors. Refer to Note 7 in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements of this report for a summary of commitments outstanding as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025.

Net interest income.text: Our results of operations depend primarily on our net interest income. Net interest income is the difference between the interest income we earn on our interest-earning assets and the interest we pay on our interest-bearing liabilities. Our results of operations also are affected by our provision for credit losses, noninterest income and noninterest expense. Noninterest income consists primarily of fees and service charges on deposit accounts, income from bank-owned life insurance and other income. Noninterest expense consists primarily of expenses related to salaries and employee benefits, occupancy and equipment, data processing, contracted services, legal and professional fees, advertising, deposit and general insurance and other expenses.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text: Noninterest income increased $11.7 million to $1.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a loss of $10.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025 as a result of $11.8 million in losses on the sale of securities from a securities repositioning strategy executed during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

intro.text: CB Financial Services, Inc. (the “Company”), a Pennsylvania corporation, is a bank holding company headquartered in Carmichaels, Pennsylvania. The Company’s common stock is traded on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol “CBFV.” The Company conducts its operations primarily through its wholly owned subsidiary, Community Bank, a Pennsylvania-chartered commercial bank. At December 31, 2025, the Company, on a consolidated basis, had total assets of $1.55 billion, total liabilities of $1.39 billion and stockholders’ equity of $157.5 million.

s.t: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Investments

The Company makes equity investments in an entity that sponsors affordable housing and other community development projects that qualify for the Low Income Housing Tax Credit ("LIHTC") program pursuant to Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code.
The Company makes equity investments in an entity that sponsors rehabilitation projects that qualify for the Historical Tax Credit ("HTC") program pursuant to Section 47 of the Internal Revenue Code.

accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
